body:
> Those images have no visual difference from a human eye.

It's not always accurate, look at this diff [base](https://s3.amazonaws.com/argos-screenshots-us/cbef82b9e9e7f1538580470506ca2074)...[compare](https://s3.amazonaws.com/argos-screenshots-us/08df1ca01f03e27ba45539c470246525), the image rendered is definitely different.

> having to configure DOM selectors is painful for an issue that should be handled at the core of your tool.

It depends on the responsibility/problem solved by the tool given the structure used. In our case, Argos-CI has the opportunity to better handle part of the flakiness, that's something we should prioritize as providing more value. But visual regression testing is hard, people will always have to do work on there side, for instance, not rendering non-deterministic data. We have a good example here, we have to hide the roundtrip time.

> Can you remind us the exact issue? Is it because we are taking screenshots as JPG instead of PNG?

I can't tell what's the source of the issue is given the information I have. It could be from the most likely to the less:

* Nondeterministic JPG image rendering, variating hardware like GPU, drivers, browser version
* Nondeterministic JPG image source
